title: The deck plan is the most honest document you get.
subtitle: What sits above and below your bed decides the voyage.

sub: A cabin is not a room. It is a position inside a steel building, and noise in a steel building travels vertically. The brochure photograph shows none of that.

title: Four things to look up, not out

items.head: The pool deck above you
items.body: Loungers dragged across steel at six in the morning. No carpet up there, and no mercy either.

items.head: The galley or crew stair below
items.body: Trolleys, hatches and a working corridor that runs quietly all night, but runs.

items.head: The show lounge one deck down
items.body: Bass carries through a floor plate long after the applause has finished.

items.head: The anchor, right forward
items.body: Weighing it at dawn in a tender port is not a sound anybody sleeps through.

points.label: Under the pool deck
points.value: A wake-up call at six on every sea day. The cheapest quiet you will ever lose.

points.label: Above the show lounge
points.value: Serene by day, and a drum kit through the floor by half past nine.

points.label: Beside the lift lobby
points.value: Footfall and conversation in both directions, at every hour.

points.label: Two decks down, mid
points.value: The quiet buy almost nobody thinks to ask for.

text: Choose the position first. The category second.
sub: Category is a price band. Position is the experience. I settle the position first, then take the cheapest category sitting inside it — rarely the cabin anyone was shown.

title: Send this to whoever you'd share a cabin with.
body: Or tell me the sailing you're holding and I'll read the deck plan properly: which cabins I'd take, which I'd refuse, and why. Complimentary.
